s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of a painless swelling over a pacemaker site with persistent systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painless swelling over the pacemaker site
Persistent fatigue, dyspnea, and cough after COVID-19 infection
Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device on chest ultrasound
key_facts: 70-year-old man with a history of nicotine use
Remote history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Remote history of bladder urothelial carcinoma
Dual-chamber pacemaker implantation for sick sinus syndrome 9 months prior
Normal pacemaker function and clinically unremarkable pocket at postoperative checks
Tested positive for COVID-19 infection three weeks before presentation
Fatigue, dyspnea, and cough persisted and worsened after COVID-19 infection
New swelling over the pacemaker site reported at a routine cardiology visit
Normal blood pressure and heart rate on examination
No signs of cardiac decompensation or cachexia
Chest ultrasound revealed a soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device
CT imaging confirmed a soft-tissue mass around the pacemaker pocket
Haematoma or infection was excluded

shortlist.label: Pacemaker pocket tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Painless swelling over pacemaker site with imaging confirmation of a soft tissue mass

shortlist.label: Metastatic laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma and new swelling at pacemaker site

shortlist.label: Metastatic bladder urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of bladder urothelial carcinoma and new swelling at pacemaker site

shortlist.label: Soft tissue sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Imaging confirmation of a soft tissue mass surrounding the pacemaker pocket

shortlist.label: Angiosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive nature and potential for rapid growth, consistent with the patient's symptoms

raw.rationale: The presence of a soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the pacemaker device, as confirmed by chest ultrasound and CT imaging, along with the exclusion of haematoma or infection, supports the diagnosis of a pacemaker pocket tumor.

rejected.label: Metastatic laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma is remote (7 years prior) and the current presentation is localized to the pacemaker site.

rejected.label: Metastatic bladder urothelial carcinoma
rejected.why: The history of bladder urothelial carcinoma is remote (10 years prior) and the current presentation is localized to the pacemaker site.

rejected.label: Soft tissue sarcoma
rejected.why: While possible, the specific location and association with the pacemaker pocket make pacemaker pocket tumor a more specific and likely diagnosis.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided to suggest angiosarcoma, such as rapid growth or metastasis, and the diagnosis of pacemaker pocket tumor is more directly supported by the findings.
